title: Separated and locally quasi-finite morphisms are stable under base change (Stacks 01KU, 01TM)
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ and $g:S'\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $f':X'=X\times_SS'\to S'$ the base change [def-pc-fibre-product]. (1) If $f$ is separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], then $f'$ is separated. (2) If $f$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite], then $f'$ is locally quasi-finite.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma Tag 01KU (lemma-separated-permanence), line 4289, item (3); Morphisms (literature/stacks-project/morphisms.tex), Lemma Tag 01TM (lemma-base-change-quasi-finite), line 3925, item (2)

proof.text: *(1).* Assume $f$ separated. Then the second projection $f':X\times_SS'\to S'$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change] (Stacks proof: the diagonal $\Delta_{f'}$ is the base change of $\Delta_f$ along $S'\to S$, and closed immersions are stable under base change).

source.place: Schemes, Lemma Tag 01KU (lemma-separated-permanence), line 4289, item (3), proof lines 4312-4327

proof.text: *(2), finite type.* Assume $f$ locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Then $f$ is locally of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-locally-finite-type], hence so is its base change $f'$ [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change]. (This is the clause 'combined with the fact that $f'$ is also locally of finite type by Lemma 01T4' of the source; the standing hypothesis 'X locally of finite type over S' of 01TM is thus implied by local quasi-finiteness.)

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01TM (lemma-base-change-quasi-finite), line 3925, item (2); proof lines 3946-3950

proof.text: *(2), a point upstairs.* Let $x'\in X'$, $g':X'\to X$ the first projection, $x=g'(x')$, $s'=f'(x')$ and $s=f(x)=g(s')$. Since $f$ is locally quasi-finite it is quasi-finite at $x$ [pqf-def-quasifinite], and $f$ is locally of finite type (step 2), so the point of the fibre $X_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] over $x$ is isolated in $X_s$ [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-at-point-isolated]. By [lem-weil-pbc-isolated-fibre-point-base-change] (applied to $f$, $g$, $x'$; it needs only $f$ locally of finite type), $x'$ is an isolated point of the fibre $X'_{s'}=X'\times_{S'}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s')$ of $f'$ at $s'$, i.e. the point of $X'_{s'}$ over $x'$ is isolated. (This is the algebra result Tag 00PP that the source invokes, in the fibre form of Tag 01TH (1)$\Leftrightarrow$(2).)

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01TM (lemma-base-change-quasi-finite), line 3925, item (2); proof lines 3946-3950

proof.text: *(2), an affine pair around $x'$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] applied to $S'$ with $W=S'$ there is an affine open $V'\subseteq S'$ with $s'\in V'$, $V'\cong\operatorname{Spec}R'$, $R'=\mathcal O_{S'}(V')$; since $f'$ is continuous, $f'^{-1}(V')$ is an open subset of $X'$ containing $x'$, and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] applied to $X'$ with $W=f'^{-1}(V')$ gives an affine open $U'\subseteq X'$ with $x'\in U'\subseteq f'^{-1}(V')$, $U'\cong\operatorname{Spec}A'$, $A'=\mathcal O_{X'}(U')$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; thus $f'(U')\subseteq V'$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01TM (lemma-base-change-quasi-finite), line 3925, item (2); proof lines 3946-3950

proof.text: *(2), conclusion.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-isolated-fibre-point-quasi-finite-affine-pairs] to $f'$ (locally of finite type by step 2), the point $x'$ (isolated in its fibre by step 3) and the affine pair $U'\ni x'$, $V'$ of step 4: the ring map $R'\to A'$ induced by $f'$ is of finite type and quasi-finite at the prime $\mathfrak q'\subset A'$ of $x'$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. This is the definition of '$f'$ quasi-finite at $x'$' [pqf-def-quasifinite] (1). As $x'\in X'$ was arbitrary, $f'$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite] (2).

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01TM (lemma-base-change-quasi-finite), line 3925, item (2); proof lines 3946-3950
